title: Functions & procedures
examples: When should I use a function instead of a procedure?
What is the difference between passing by value and passing by reference?
Can a function have multiple return values?

explain.say: Today we are learning about functions and procedures in programming.
A function often needs information to do its job.
Parameters are like ingredients a recipe needs to start.
Some functions calculate something and give an answer back.
The return value is the final result the function sends back.
Scope tells us where a variable name can be seen in the code.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a function and a procedure?
faq.a: A function usually calculates and sends back a specific value. A procedure just performs an action without necessarily returning a value.
asks: When should I use a function vs a procedure?
Does a procedure always do something?

faq.q: If I pass a parameter, does the original variable change?
faq.a: This depends on how the language handles it, but generally, you must be aware if the original data can be modified inside the function.
asks: Can parameters change my original data?

faq.a: Scope defines the region of the code where a variable name is valid and can be used. Variables outside their scope cause errors.
asks: Why do I get a 'variable not found' error?

faq.q: Can I use a function if I don't need to return anything?
faq.a: Yes, you can. In that case, it acts more like a procedure, just using the function structure for organization.
asks: Is it okay to write a function with no return?
What if the function just prints something?

faq.q: How many parameters can a function take?
faq.a: Most programming languages allow functions to take any number of parameters you define for them.
asks: Can a function take many inputs?
Is there a limit on parameters?

facts: Parameters act as placeholders for data when a function is called.
A return value is the single piece of data a function sends back to the caller.
Local scope means a variable only exists while the function runs.
Using functions helps prevent repeating the same code many times.

quiz.say: If a function calculates the area using length and width, what are length and width?
quiz.why: Parameters are the inputs the function needs to perform its calculation.

wrong.0: A procedure is the whole block of code, not the specific inputs.
wrong.2: The return value is the final answer, not the inputs.
wrong.3: Scope describes where a variable can be seen, not what it is.

quiz.say: If a variable is declared inside a function, where can it be accessed?
quiz.why: Local scope means the variable only exists while that specific function is running.

wrong.0: While true, 'only inside the function' is the more precise term for local scope.
wrong.2: Global means it can be used everywhere, which is not true for local variables.
wrong.3: This is too restrictive; it can be used in other functions too.

quiz.say: Which term describes the final result sent back by a function?
quiz.why: The return value is the specific output the function passes back to the part of the program that called it.

wrong.0: Scope is about visibility, not the data being sent back.
wrong.1: A procedure call is the action of running the code, not the result.
wrong.3: Parameters are the data given to the function at the start.
